title: Bind artifact metadata to actual candidate bytes
statement: The system shall describe each candidate artifact using factual source, generator, version, target, inventory, integrity, and observed-validation information that agrees with the actual artifact bytes and the selected compatibility representation.

what.problem: Self-asserted metadata or a mismatched digest chain can make the wrong archive appear trustworthy.
what.desired_outcome: Consumers can verify the exact candidate and distinguish artifact facts, generated expectations, and observed checks.

why.rationale: The archive producer, installer, and release operation must agree on the artifact identity they exchange.

conditions: When candidate metadata is generated, consumed, or qualified.

contexts: Versioned target archives, npm-bundled metadata, release indexes, and their consumer verification boundary.

how.approach: Derive inventory, size, checksums, tree hashes, file counts, and source/generator identity from actual artifacts. Preserve the specified current tree-hash representation and its retained historical verification path; reject unknown algorithms before consistency checks. Keep validation intent separate from actual observed results and bind package-bundled metadata to its release index.

how_much.scope: Packaging owns exact regular-file membership, text normalization, UTF-8 ordering, hash rows, metadata fields, and versioned archive representation. Current v2 and historical v1 meanings remain distinct, including the historical meaning of a missing algorithm field. Hash exclusion does not authorize unsafe path writes.

acceptance_criteria: Artifact names, target/version, archive members, checksums, tree hashes, counts, and recorded source/generator facts agree with the inspected candidate bytes.

An unknown integrity algorithm rejects; current candidates use the declared current representation while historical trusted metadata retains its specified verification meaning without recomputation or rewriting.
A generated descriptor does not mark an unexecuted check as passed; actual validation observations identify their subject and result.
Installer-consumed bundled metadata matches the trusted release index; a changed archive, index, or metadata invalidates the prior integrity chain.
